decision_context.user: Canadian citizen, California resident filing jointly, one Adobe income, possible house in 2-3 years; Canada bullishness is a thesis to test rather than a settled fact.
decision_context.boundary: Research only. No target price, trade, allocation or tax conclusion. None of these equities is protected house capital.

currency_and_valuation.cadusd_basis: US$24.16 EFXT divided by C$33.96 EFX.TO; used only for cross-currency valuation arithmetic.
currency_and_valuation.warning: Yahoo/quote-provider EFX and BDGI EV fields are invalid because they mix CAD equity values with USD debt/EBITDA. Recomputed figures below use one currency.

EFX.identity: Enerflex Ltd.; TSX EFX / NYSE EFXT; issuer reports in USD.
EFX.confidence: VERIFIED for historical financials and contract announcements; ASSUMED for valuation scenarios and portfolio fit.
EFX.verdict: WATCH / best of these three on current evidence, but wait for award economics or a larger valuation cushion before treating the October AI-power rerating as underwritten value.

business_quality.assessment: Medium-high operating quality with a deliberately mixed model: recurring contracted EI assets and AMS service, plus cyclical/project-based ES manufacturing. FY2025 ROCE was 16.9%; leverage fell to 0.8x bank-adjusted net debt/EBITDA by Q2. Vertical integration, global installed base, engineering/fabrication capability and contract-compression fleet are credible advantages, but large-project execution and gas-industry capital spending prevent a wide-moat classification.
business_quality.growth_and_margins: Q2 revenue declined 5.4% YoY to US$582m while H1 was flat. Q2 adjusted EBITDA declined 1.5% to US$128m but H1 rose 9.1% to US$265m. Gross margin rose to 23.9% from 22.6%. ES backlog before the October awards was US$1.453b, up 18%.
business_quality.cash_and_balance_sheet: LTM company-defined FCF is approximately US$231m (FY2025 US$230m + H1'26 US$47m - H1'25 US$46m), a 7.8% yield on the recomputed equity value. Conventional CFO less PP&E/EI-asset capex is approximately US$238m (FY2025 US$345m-US$115m, plus H1'26 US$121m-US$69m, less H1'25 US$92m-US$48m). The company definition additionally deducts lease principal and mandatory debt repayments and adds disposal proceeds; both measures retain working-capital timing. Issuer-defined net debt was US$455m and excludes US$68m lease liabilities. Upcoming ES facility/capability spend of roughly US$100m and order working capital can reduce near-term conversion.
business_quality.shares_and_compensation: Diluted shares fell about 1.0% YoY in Q2, but cash/liability-based share compensation surged to US$19m in Q2 and US$41m in H1 as the stock rose. Treat adjusted EBITDA's SBC add-back as an economic cost sensitivity, not free earnings.
business_quality.governance_and_concentration: Nine of ten directors were independent, but director/officer ownership was only about 0.53%. US revenue was 45% and Canadian revenue 13% in FY2025; North America overall was 66%. The October customers are unnamed, so backlog/customer concentration and cancellation terms remain unknown.

canada_and_ai_transmission.canada: Canadian headquarters and manufacturing/engineering base do not equal domestic revenue. FY2025 Canada destination sales were only US$334m (13%). Canadian LNG/gas-egress investment can help ES, but the larger exposure is US gas production, global LNG/process infrastructure and international projects.
canada_and_ai_transmission.ai: Direct, not merely optional: official October contracts now cover more than 1.75 GW of behind-the-meter gas generation for North American data-center developments through 2028. The value chain is still physical gas-fired equipment, engineering and service rather than AI software or merchant electricity. The missing contract dollars, margins, customers and working-capital terms prevent quantifying per-share value.

valuation.shares_basis: Common shares outstanding at 2026-07-31; later share changes through the quote date were not disclosed in the reviewed primary sources.
valuation.debt_definition: Issuer net debt is long-term debt less cash and excludes current and long-term lease liabilities. Lease-inclusive EV is shown separately.
valuation.reported_pe_comment: About 55x and not decision-useful because FY2025 debt-redemption costs and SBC volatility distort reported earnings.
valuation.entry_logic: Current 6.4x LTM adjusted EBITDA is not obviously expensive, yet the stock embeds some October-award optimism without disclosed economics. A US$18-US$22 range would correspond to roughly 5-6x existing LTM EBITDA before crediting award uplift; above that, require disclosed order value/margin/cash conversion rather than an AI label. This is sensitivity, not a target.

EFX.bear_case: The October backlog could have lower margins, milestone/cancellation risk and heavy working-capital/capacity requirements; execution delays or liquidated damages would hurt cash conversion. Existing earnings remain tied to gas compression, LNG/process capex and oil/gas customers. US$41m H1 SBC, percentage-of-completion estimates, international project/arbitration risk and the prior Exterran leverage history weaken the clean-compounder case.
catalysts: Disclosure of October award dollars/margins and conversion schedule
North American LNG and gas egress buildout
recommendation_changers: Order value, gross margin and working-capital profile
A downside gas-capex stress showing FCF/debt resilience
EFX.portfolio_fit: Adds a direct data-center gas-power equipment backlog, but also increases the same gas/oil-service factor already represented by TOU/CNQ/BKR/LNG/SLB. At most a small long-horizon risk-bucket candidate after the missing award economics; it should compete with existing energy holdings rather than be called diversification.

BDGI.identity: Badger Infrastructure Solutions Ltd.; TSX BDGI; issuer reports in USD.
BDGI.confidence: VERIFIED for financials and fleet facts; ASSUMED for valuation scenarios and moat/fit judgments.
BDGI.verdict: WATCH / high-quality growth execution at a full price. Prefer a pullback or proof that elevated growth capex converts into durable per-share FCF without safety deterioration.

business_quality.assessment: A scaled North American hydrovac operator with vertical truck manufacturing, roughly 140 field locations, standardized equipment, route density and a recognized non-destructive excavation method. These are real scale advantages, but local service competition, labor/operator dependence, fleet intensity and safety exposure limit moat strength.
business_quality.growth_and_margins: Q2 organic revenue rose 23%, adjusted EBITDA 25%, and RPT 14%; fleet rose 8%. Q2 margin improved 40bp to 25.7%, while H1 margin slipped 10bp to 22.6%. Growth is broad but partly capacity/utilization/pricing rather than acquisition.
business_quality.cash_and_balance_sheet: LTM adjusted EBITDA is about US$215.9m. LTM actual CFO is about US$176.8m and capex US$163.3m, leaving about US$13.5m conventional CFO-minus-capex because of fleet growth. Issuer Total Debt/net debt of US$254.1m excludes US$73.3m lease liabilities; lease-inclusive EV/EBITDA is 11.15x. 2026 capex plus tariffs is US$188m-US$230m and excludes a second US factory.
business_quality.shares_and_compensation: Q2 diluted shares fell 0.3% YoY and buybacks continue, but Q2 SBC expense was US$21.5m, 32% of adjusted EBITDA, after the share-price increase. Derivative gains offset much of it in adjusted net income; economic dilution/cash settlement still deserves scrutiny.
business_quality.governance_and_safety: The business has 2,145 hourly employees and is rapidly hiring/training operators. AIF language acknowledges confined-space, heavy-equipment, injury/death and customer-qualification risks. No quantitative safety trend was found in the reviewed Q2/AIF sources; require TRIR/LTIR, serious incidents and turnover/training data before a quality premium is accepted.

canada_and_ai_transmission.canada: Canadian headquarters and Red Deer manufacturing are meaningful domestic activity, but economics are mostly US. At FY2025 end, about 79% of trucks and 81% of employees were US-based; issuer says most revenue is US without an exact split. A second US factory would further reduce Canadian production concentration.
canada_and_ai_transmission.ai: Indirect at most. Hydrovac supports utilities, communications, water, gas, sewer, construction and facility work; data-center/AI buildout can increase utility excavation, but no AI-attributable orders or revenue were disclosed. Treat it as utility/infrastructure capex exposure.

valuation.shares_basis: Common shares issued and outstanding at 2026-06-30; later share changes through the quote date were not disclosed in the reviewed primary sources.
valuation.debt_definition: Issuer Total Debt is long-term debt less cash and excludes lease liabilities. Lease-inclusive EV is shown separately.
valuation.entry_logic: Current valuation requires sustained double-digit growth and improved future FCF. Around C$79 corresponds to 10x LTM adjusted EBITDA; C$60-C$70 would provide a wider 8-9x cushion. Paying above C$85 should require evidence the current capex wave earns attractive incremental returns and safety/retention remain controlled. Sensitivity only, not a target.

BDGI.bear_case: Growth slows after utility/construction demand normalizes while a larger fleet, new service lines and second factory lock in depreciation, labor and lease costs. US truck tariffs already add US$18m-US$30m to 2026 capital. FCF is currently minimal after capex, SBC is high, and a serious safety incident could impair customers, costs and reputation.
catalysts: Second US plant lowering tariff/logistics friction
North American utility and infrastructure capex
recommendation_changers: Incremental return on new trucks and service lines
BDGI.portfolio_fit: More distinct from existing energy producers/services than EFX because demand spans utilities and civil infrastructure. It is still a high-multiple, capital-intensive cyclical service equity with mostly US economics, and therefore a poor Canada-domestic or house-capital hedge.

CF.identity: Canaccord Genuity Group Inc.; TSX CF; financial-services issuer reporting in CAD.
CF.confidence: VERIFIED for issuer metrics; ASSUMED for normalized earnings and fit judgments.
CF.verdict: WATCH / unconfirmed special situation. Current adjusted earnings look cheap and a UK wealth liquidity event could surface substantial attributable value, but no primary source confirms a sale or its waterfall. Do not classify it as an industrial Build Canada investment or capitalize gross rumored proceeds.

business_quality.assessment: A diversified independent investment bank and wealth manager. Wealth management's C$160.2b client assets, advisor relationships and recurring fees reduce—but do not eliminate—capital-markets cyclicality. The franchise depends on people, market levels, financing/advisory closings and compensation discipline; five-year adjusted EPS varied from C$0.40 to C$2.51.
business_quality.growth_and_margins: Q1 adjusted revenue rose 28.8% and adjusted common income nearly tripled. Wealth revenue rose 25.6% and capital-markets revenue 30.2%. Australia includes acquisition growth; advisory and financing activity are episodic. Compensation rose to 62.6% of revenue, absorbing much of operating leverage.
business_quality.capital_and_balance_sheet: Industrial net-debt/FCF analysis is inappropriate. Broker/dealer settlement balances, securities inventory/shorts and regulatory capital dominate cash flow. At March 2026 shareholders' equity was C$780.6m including C$205.6m preferred equity; NCI C$433.8m, bank loans C$464.5m and convertible debentures C$90.0m. UK and Australian subsidiaries have material outside ownership.
business_quality.shares_and_compensation: Issued shares rose 0.25% in Q1; RSU grants, LTIP trust activity, convertible debt and subsidiary preferred interests complicate dilution. Firm compensation was 60% of FY2026 revenue and 62.6% in Q1.
business_quality.governance_and_conflicts: Insider ownership (10.7%) and the 14.3% employee partnership align employees, but much is company-financed. The circular disclosed C$79.1m share-purchase loans, C$197.4m other insider indebtedness and a C$5m forgivable executive loan. The failed 2023 management take-private, complex NCI structures, research/underwriting/investing conflicts and 2026 US$80m AML settlement warrant a governance discount.

canada_and_ai_transmission.canada: Only 34.7% of FY2026 revenue was Canadian. Build-Canada transmission is indirect through Canadian wealth, financing/advisory and especially metals/mining activity: metals/mining was 51% of global underwriting revenue and 11% of advisory revenue. Those sector shares are global and include issuers outside Canadian infrastructure.
canada_and_ai_transmission.ai: No disclosed AI-attributable revenue. Technology was 13% of underwriting and 52% of advisory revenue, but technology is not synonymous with AI. The annual outlook mentions AI-infrastructure investment as macro support and the AIF discusses AI chiefly as operational/cyber/model risk.

uk_wealth_sale_special_situation.primary_status_as_of_cutoff: UNCONFIRMED. The issuer's press-release archive through 2026-10-20 contains no announced UK wealth sale, signed agreement, buyer, valuation, proceeds allocation, retained stake, tax estimate or closing conditions. The interview explicitly described media circulation and said a sale might be forthcoming; it did not claim an issuer-announced deal.
uk_wealth_sale_special_situation.why_a_process_is_plausible: The 2021 CGWM UK convertible preferred terms provide outside holders liquidity rights after the fifth anniversary. At June 2026, Canaccord held an approximate 66.9% equity-equivalent interest; convertible preferred, preference and management/employee interests represented 33.1%, subject to liquidation preferences. A management incentive plan can also pay on a liquidity event.
uk_wealth_sale_special_situation.current_unit_facts: Q1 FY2027 UK & Crown Dependencies client assets were C$81.7b/£43.4b, revenue C$130.6m, adjusted pre-tax income C$29.2m and normalized EBITDA £23.0m. Approximate LTM normalized EBITDA is £90m (FY2026 £88m + Q1 FY2027 £23m - inferred Q1 FY2026 £21.1m). CGWM UK acquisition bank debt was C$450.0m at June 30, approximately £239m using the filing-implied C$1.882/£ from client assets.
uk_wealth_sale_special_situation.sensitivity_method_and_limits: For each scenario: subtract approximately £239m CGWM UK debt from whole-unit EV, apply CF's 66.9% simple as-converted share, translate at C$1.882/£ and divide by 103.02m shares. This is a gross, pre-tax, pre-fee illustration—not distributable proceeds. It does not model the convertible preferred liquidation preference, accrued dividends, management incentive, transaction costs, tax, EFG Harris Allday consideration, working/regulatory capital retained in the unit, or any retained stake. Minority holders' 33.1% and their preference rights are not CF common equity.
uk_wealth_sale_special_situation.headline_rumor_guardrail: A media headline valuation cannot be underwritten from primary sources. If a quoted £1.0b were enterprise value, the simple bridge would imply about C$959m/C$9.30 per CF share attributable before the listed deductions; if it were equity value, the result would differ materially. The issuer has verified neither the number nor its definition.
uk_wealth_sale_special_situation.recent_primary_releases: On August 18, CGWM UK agreed to acquire EFG Harris Allday's front-office teams and £3.1b client assets; 2025 revenue was £20.3m, consideration was undisclosed and closing was expected in H2 2026. On August 24, CF announced redemption of all Series A preferred shares for C$113.5m cash on October 1. These affect cash, debt and the perimeter of any SOTP; neither release confirms a UK sale.
uk_wealth_sale_special_situation.deal_probability: Speculative rather than zero: contractual liquidity rights and media circulation are consistent with a process, but changing reported bidder names and the absence of primary terms prevent assigning a defensible closing probability or sale value. Do not capitalize proceeds until a definitive issuer announcement supplies structure and waterfall.

valuation.shares_basis: Common shares issued and outstanding at 2026-06-30; this includes shares held in employee trusts and does not model subsequent vesting or convertible dilution.
valuation.entry_logic: C$13.47 is inexpensive only if the recent C$1.49 adjusted LTM run rate is durable or a UK liquidity event realizes an attractive attributable value. On C$1.00 mid-cycle EPS it is 13.5x. The separate UK SOTP sensitivity implies roughly C$5.88-C$10.28 per CF share at 8x-12x whole-unit EV/LTM EBITDA before taxes, fees, preferences and incentives, but the remaining group is not free: it carries cyclicality, corporate costs, preferred/convertible claims and regulatory risk. A C$9-C$11 price would offer a clearer mid-cycle margin absent a deal. Sensitivity only, not a target.

CF.bear_case: Markets/AUM fall and financing/advisory closings retreat, compressing revenue while compensation remains sticky. Adjusted earnings exclude a long list of acquisition, incentive, fair-value, legal and impairment items; the US goodwill impairment and US$80m AML settlement show some are economically real. Convertibles, preferred equity, NCI and company-financed employee ownership dilute/complicate common-holder returns.
catalysts: A definitive UK wealth transaction with an attributable proceeds waterfall
Sustained wealth net inflows and higher recurring mix
Completion of AML lookback without added sanction
recommendation_changers: Issuer-confirmed UK sale EV/equity-value definition, retained stake, tax, debt repayment, preference/incentive waterfall and use of proceeds
A clean through-cycle common EPS bridge
Fully diluted common ownership and subsidiary NCI waterfall
CF.portfolio_fit: Overlaps BRK/FFH only at the broad financial-sector label; economically it is a much smaller, higher-beta, compensation-heavy investment bank/wealth manager. It adds cyclic capital-markets exposure rather than defensive financial quality. Any position must compete with existing financial holdings and stay outside house capital.

cross_company_ranking.reason: Best current valuation and cash yield, manageable debt, and newly verified direct data-center power backlog. Main gap is award economics; energy-factor overlap is high.
Best apparent organic operating momentum and differentiated hydrovac scale, but mostly US economics, heavy capex, missing safety KPIs and a much fuller valuation.

Cheapest headline adjusted P/E and an explicit UK-wealth special situation, but the sale is unconfirmed and gross proceeds are not CF common equity. Cyclical/complex earnings, regulatory/governance baggage and weak direct Build Canada/AI transmission keep it third pending a definitive attributable-value waterfall.

thesis_conclusion: Canadian listing/domicile is a poor exposure proxy across all three. EFX is chiefly US/global gas infrastructure with now-direct North American data-center power backlog; BDGI is a Canadian-manufactured but mostly US hydrovac operator; CF is a global financial intermediary with only about one-third Canadian revenue. The evidence supports selective company underwriting, not a blanket Canada rerating thesis.
